title: ChatGPT can peek at your Chrome tabs now
slides: ChatGPT can now read your open Chrome tabs. Should it?
The feature connects directly to your browser session
It also remembers what you were working on earlier
You must manually approve each tab it reads
Disable tab access when you finish a task
thread_text:
1. Your browser is now a plugin

ChatGPT can read every open Chrome tab. The feature connects directly to your session, so it sees what you see — no copy-paste required.

2. It remembers your mess

Beyond live tabs, it also recalls what you were working on earlier. That context persists across sessions, turning casual browsing into a searchable memory.

3. You control the gate

Every tab must be manually approved before ChatGPT reads it. No auto-scan. But approval fatigue is real — you might click yes without thinking.

4. The privacy trade-off

Approving a tab means sharing cookies, logins, and sensitive data. One wrong click and your banking session enters the chat.

5. Lock it down today

After finishing a task, disable tab access in ChatGPT settings. Does your workflow really need permanent browser memory? Test it on one project this week.

instagram.caption:
ChatGPT can now read the Chrome tabs you have open, straight from your browser session.

You approve each tab manually, so no silent scanning. But approving shares cookies and logins with it.

It also remembers what you were working on earlier, turning casual browsing into persistent memory.

If you write or publish for a living, every research tab you approve during a task stays in that context.

Try it on one project this week, then check your ChatGPT settings: do you still want that tab access on? 🔒👀
